financial_lines: Screenprint on Limoges or Moustiers porcelain from a design after a watercolor by the artist. - Signed bottom centre, 1986 - 25 cm diameter - Excellent condition - Zao Wou-Ki & Ateliers de Ségriès - Produced for the BSN group on the occasion of its twentieth anniversary in 1986 by the Ateliers de Ségriès in Moustiers, commissioned from Zao Wou-Ki by his friend Antoine Ribou. Zao Wou-Ki was born in Beijing on February 1, 1920. In 1935, he passed the entrance exam for the Hangzhou School of Fine Arts, where he was appointed lecturer after six years of study; he held his first exhibition in 1941 in Chiang Kai-shek. It was in 1948 that he decided to settle in Paris.

Screenprint from 1982 depicting the iconic British comic-strip character Andy Capp, rendered through Estes’s crisp photorealist sensibility. Published during a period when Estes was extending his vocabulary beyond urban storefronts into popular imagery, the print balances graphic clarity with subtle spatial depth. Literature reference: J. Arthur, Richard Estes: Painting and Prints, Pomegranate Artbooks, 1993, pp. 125–126.

Lithograph from 1925 depicting a seated female reader holding a bouquet of roses. Catalogued as Duthuit 471. The composition exemplifies Matisse’s early mastery of line and contour, combining interior calm with decorative balance. Executed during a formative decade in which Matisse refined his graphic language alongside painting and sculpture.
